newsitem.title: UK: OPEC president calls for output restraint - Lukman.
newsitem.headline: OPEC president calls for output restraint - Lukman.

text.p: The president of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), Libya's oil minister Abdalla el-Badri, has called on its members to restrain oil output to help support sagging crude prices, OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman said on Monday.
It is not yet clear whether there has been any response to the request, he added.
"The president has been calling and asking members to exercise restraint," Lukman told Reuters on the sidelines of an industry conference.
"We will have to wait and see," whether member countries would respond, Lukman added.
OPEC sources said in early April that el-Badri had consulted on the telephone with other OPEC ministers to discuss the slide in world oil markets.

OPEC output, estimated in a Reuters survey at 26.9 million bpd in March, has risen by about a million bpd in the past year and is approaching two million bpd above the group's official 25.03 million ceiling.
Output has risen for several months in succession, led by increased production from Iraq under the humanitarian oil-for-food exchange supervised by the United Nations.
But a number of other OPEC producers -- in particular Venezuela, Nigeria and Qatar -- have been pumping hugely in excess of official allocations.
The value of benchmark Brent blend fell from just below $25 in early January to a low of $17.54 in early April. Prices have since stabilised and Brent was trading at $18.14 a barrel on Monday.
Lukman is due to attend a regular meeting of OPEC's ministerial output monitoring committee on May 6-7 in Isfahan, Iran.
The committee is currently chaired by Iran's Gholamreza Aghazadeh and also comprises Indonesia's Ida Bagus Sudjana and Nigeria's Dan Etete.
